title: Justice and defence-procurement research
scope: Selected public evidence and executable follow-up tests; no exhaustive network or hidden-coordination finding.

sources.title: PAC Fiftieth Report: Management of Defence Offsets (18th Lok Sabha)
sources.publisher: Lok Sabha Secretariat / Public Accounts Committee
sources.supports: Part I paras 15,18,19,21: separate portfolio snapshots; paras 29–35: oversight; para 54(iv): Alpha relationships. Part II introduction: institutional roles.
sources.limitations: Ministry testimony and committee observations must be distinguished. Contract-level evidence and hearing minutes are absent; minutes explicitly not appended.

sources.title: Management of Defence Offsets: PRS report summary
sources.supports: Original summary used by the earlier dossier; acquisition pathway and denominator comparison.
sources.limitations: Same underlying PAC report; not independent confirmation. Original tables now govern numeric interpretation.

sources.title: Adani Enterprises Annual Report 2018–19
sources.supports: Consolidated entity table, printed pp 205,207, entries 105,158: AEL→ADSTL 100%; ADSTL→Alpha 26%. Printed p. 265 dates Alpha associate entry 13 Dec 2018.
sources.limitations: Historical 31 Mar 2019 ownership snapshot; does not establish 2026 shareholding, beneficial interests beyond the filing, or improper award influence.

sources.title: Ministry of Defence: Year End Review 2020
sources.publisher: Ministry of Defence / Press Information Bureau
sources.supports: Defence Offset Policy 2020 section: policy objectives and vendors selecting Indian offset partners.
sources.limitations: Government policy account from 2020, not an independent performance audit or complete current rulebook.

sources.title: Vihaan Kumar v State of Haryana, 2025 INSC 162
sources.supports: Paras 24–33: grounds to the arrested person; arrest invalidated; merits reserved; Haryana instructions directed.
sources.limitations: Case-specific remedy. Subsequent trial and compliance outcomes not acquired. The Court did not decide the 24-hour issue.

sources.title: Mihir Rajesh Shah v State of Maharashtra, 2025 INSC 1288
sources.supports: Paras 52–58: written grounds; exceptional oral-first procedure; two-hour minimum before remand; prospective application.
sources.limitations: Version inspected has operative conclusions at paras 52–58; later Jaskaran judgment refers to differently numbered paragraphs. Preserve each version locator.

sources.title: Jaskaran Jeet Singh Deol v State of Punjab, 2026 INSC 1022
sources.supports: Paras 24–25.1,36,38–39: judicial approval for re-arrest, supervisory endorsement and departmental inquiry; application to Article 22(2); merits reserved.
sources.limitations: This is the inspected 21 Sep 2026 judgment, not a complete later docket check. Compensation is fact-dependent under para 36; no automatic compensation amount.

sources.title: Prabir Purkayastha v State (NCT of Delhi), 2024 INSC 414
sources.supports: Paras 38–50: invalid arrest/remand; para 44 reserves merits. Judgment extends written-ground reasoning across PMLA/UAPA context.
sources.limitations: Not an acquittal; does not dispose of every NewsClick proceeding. Counsel allegations in earlier paragraphs are not Court findings.

sources.title: Manohar Lal Sharma v Union of India: technical inquiry order
sources.publisher: Supreme Court of India; judgment reproduced by LiveLaw
sources.supports: Paras 55–62: independent technical committee, specified inquiry questions, authority to call records, Union/state support.
sources.limitations: Order establishes inquiry architecture, not operator attribution. Full subsequent technical report and current official docket not acquired.

connections.label: PAC examined offset management
connections.summary: The 2026 report examines the ministry’s offset administration.
limits: Parliamentary scrutiny is not a criminal finding.
alternativeExplanations: Delivery or verification failures can arise without collusion.
connections.falsifier: A corrected official report contradicting the recorded subject or responsible department.

connections.label: DOMW monitors offset fulfilment
connections.summary: Part II identifies DOMW within Defence Production as the monitoring office.
limits: A formal reporting line does not establish political direction of any particular decision.
connections.falsifier: Authoritative delegation records assigning the relevant function elsewhere.

connections.label: CGDA verifies vendor claims
connections.summary: Part II identifies CGDA as internal verifier of claims.
limits: Verification, acceptance and payment remain separate.
alternativeExplanations: Pending claims may await adequate documentation.
connections.falsifier: The applicable contract and delegation record assigns a different verifier.

connections.label: USD 9,237.64 m claimed at 14 Jan 2026
limits: This is a portfolio total, not a transfer to DOMW or an accepted-delivery total.
alternativeExplanations: Amendments and claim corrections may alter aggregates.
connections.falsifier: A reconciled contract-level register contradicts the table.

connections.label: 100% holding at 31 Mar 2019
connections.summary: The 2019 consolidated entity table records ADSTL as a 100%-owned AEL subsidiary, entry 105.
limits: Historical snapshot only; dateFrom marks the observation date, not incorporation or present ownership.
alternativeExplanations: Corporate ownership is an ordinary business relationship.
connections.falsifier: A corrected 2019 filing or contemporaneous share register contradicting this entry.

connections.label: 26% associate holding at 31 Mar 2019
connections.summary: Entry 158 records Alpha as a 26% associate held by ADSTL; the report dates its associate entry 13 Dec 2018.
limits: Do not label the 2019 position wholly-owned or controlling; subsequent ownership changes are outside this snapshot.
alternativeExplanations: A minority investment can fund manufacturing capacity.
connections.falsifier: A corrected filing or contemporaneous register disproves the 26% holding.

connections.label: Alpha named as MBDA offset partner
connections.summary: Ministry evidence names Alpha as an MBDA offset partner for missiles.
limits: Individual contract IDs and delivered-credit ledgers were not acquired.
connections.falsifier: Primary contract or vendor confirmation contradicts the relationship.

connections.label: Alpha named as IAI offset partner
connections.summary: The same evidence names an offset relationship for radars.
limits: The source’s entity name is retained pending legal-entity identifier verification.
connections.falsifier: Primary contracts identify a different legal entity or disprove the relationship.

connections.label: MHA police/paramilitary clientele reported
connections.summary: The ministry lists MHA police/paramilitary projects among Alpha’s clientele.
limits: No project identifiers, procurement routes or payment evidence inspected.
alternativeExplanations: Defence suppliers also supply civilian security agencies.
connections.falsifier: Award and acceptance records disprove the named clientele.

connections.label: Vendor choice of offset partners
connections.summary: The 2020 policy summary states that vendors choose their Indian offset partners.
limits: Historical policy summary; contract-specific eligibility and later amendments govern each transaction.
alternativeExplanations: Partner choice can reflect capability, cost and commercial strategy.
connections.falsifier: Applicable contract terms establish different selection responsibility.

connections.label: Vihaan arrest invalidated
connections.summary: The Court invalidated the arrest for non-communication of grounds and directed Haryana to issue safeguards.
limits: Underlying charges were expressly unaffected; Article 22(2) issue was not decided.
alternativeExplanations: Procedural noncompliance does not by itself establish a coordinated campaign.
connections.falsifier: A later operative order changes the remedy or a corrected judgment changes the holding.

connections.label: Purkayastha arrest/remand invalidated
connections.summary: The 2024 decision invalidated arrest and remand in FIR 224/2023 for failure to supply grounds in time.
limits: Merits were reserved; separate EOW/PMLA/FEMA matters require their own records.
alternativeExplanations: A procedural failure can occur without proof of fabricated substantive accusations.
connections.falsifier: A later operative order reverses this procedural disposition.

connections.label: Written grounds across offences
connections.summary: Mihir requires understandable written grounds; exceptional oral-first arrests require writing within reasonable time and at least two hours before remand.
limits: Paras 52–58 apply prospectively; do not retroactively score every earlier arrest against the new schedule.
alternativeExplanations: Urgent witnessed offences can justify the specified oral-first exception.
connections.falsifier: A later binding larger-bench ruling or legislation validly alters the applicable rule.

connections.label: Judicial approval after unconstitutional arrest
connections.summary: Paras 24–25 require furnished grounds, a justified application endorsed by a superior and magistrate approval for re-arrest after release for Article 22(1) breach.
limits: This is not blanket immunity from investigation or subsequent lawful arrest.
alternativeExplanations: A documented bona fide need can support renewed custody under supervision.
connections.falsifier: A later binding order changes these safeguards.

connections.label: New investigator and departmental inquiry
connections.summary: Para 25.1 requires reassignment and departmental inquiry in this re-arrest process; para 36 extends the process to Article 22(2) breaches.
limits: A final adverse disciplinary finding must precede disciplinary consequences; merits of the accusation were not decided.
alternativeExplanations: Documented remedial compliance may correct the original failure.
connections.falsifier: Implementation records or subsequent judicial orders disprove claimed compliance or alter the direction.

connections.label: Independent Pegasus technical inquiry
connections.summary: The 2021 order appoints an independent technical committee supervised by a former Supreme Court judge.
limits: An inquiry appointment is not proof of a particular operator or unlawful infection.
alternativeExplanations: Foreign operators, attribution errors or unrelated malware remain possibilities to test.
connections.falsifier: Authenticated final findings reject the proposed attribution or an official correction changes the inquiry scope.

connections.label: Committee authorised to request records
connections.summary: Paras 61–62 authorise inquiry into procurement/authority questions and calling records; Union/state agencies must support it.
limits: The full technical report and a comprehensive current docket were not obtained.
alternativeExplanations: Some records can require lawful redaction while still supporting independent review.
connections.falsifier: An authentic disclosed report or production log establishes the specific request was satisfied or outside scope.

leads.title: Reconcile offset snapshots before calculating failure
leads.question: Why does the reported claim total decrease between the two dated PAC tables, and do all status amounts share one denominator?
neededEvidence: A versioned DOMW export matching each table date with stable contract/claim IDs.
Separate contracted, due, submitted, credited, rejected, withdrawn, penalty-imposed and penalty-recovered amounts.
Written reconciliation of the status-category totals and any corrections.
disconfirmingEvidence: Documented scope changes, withdrawn duplicate claims, currency conversions or a formal corrigendum explain the residuals.
leads.feasibility: High for table reproduction (completed); medium for public aggregate reconciliation; contract-level release depends on lawful disclosure.

leads.title: Test acceptance and penalty enforcement
leads.question: Among matured obligations, are credits or waivers unsupported after amendments, multipliers and acceptance evidence are reconciled?
neededEvidence: Complete maturity cohort including all vendors, successful claims and rejected claims.
Acceptance certificates; amended schedules; original claim documents; penalty assessment, recovery and waiver orders.
Independent technical sample confirming deliverables and allowed valuation.
disconfirmingEvidence: Accepted deliverables, justified extensions and consistently applied valuation rules reconcile the suspected exceptions.
Penalty collections or lawful waiver reasons account for assessed amounts.
leads.feasibility: Medium: aggregate oversight documents are public; a complete transactional cohort is not yet available.

leads.title: Resolve the arms-to-police supplier bridge
leads.question: Which actual awards underlie the Alpha/MBDA/IAI/MHA relationships, and what was the ownership at each award date?
neededEvidence: Public contract IDs, award dates, tender notices and scope; corresponding legal company identifiers.
Contemporaneous ownership records, amendments and disclosed subcontractor roles.
Complete comparable procurement set, including losing bidders and awards to unconnected firms.
disconfirmingEvidence: Competitively justified awards and verified deliveries explain the relationships without improper influence.
Historical relationships ended before the decision being studied, or supposed entities are different legal companies.
leads.feasibility: Medium: corporate chronology is feasible; some security procurement detail may be withheld lawfully. A commercial relationship alone supplies no corruption allegation.

leads.title: Measure safeguards across agencies and governments
leads.question: After each rule’s effective date, which agencies and remand courts persistently fail meaningful grounds service, and are corrections documented?
neededEvidence: Pre-specified complete published-order cohort, both compliant and noncompliant decisions, with defined missing-data rules.
Grounds-service and remand timestamps; exception reasons; supervisory endorsements and reassignment orders where lawfully public.
Separate ordinary-law, UAPA and PMLA cohorts, case severity/stage, state and legal-version controls.
disconfirmingEvidence: Failures fall after training; no excess remains relative to matched offices and cases.
Contemporaneous proof establishes timely service and lawful exception handling.
leads.feasibility: High for a reproducible published-judgment sample; low for a population claim without unpublished remand and arrest denominators.

leads.title: Complete the surveillance accountability record
leads.question: What can a lawful redacted technical report establish about infection, operator, procurement and authority as separate questions?
neededEvidence: Official docket and disclosure orders after the previously inspected hearings.
Redacted committee findings, lawful production logs, independent forensic methods and chain-of-custody summaries.
Procurement and authorisation records connected by precise dates and identifiers.
disconfirmingEvidence: Validated re-analysis rejects a claimed infection or assigns it to a different operator.
Independently reviewed authorisations establish lawful scope for the specific incident.
leads.feasibility: Limited until primary committee output is public; do not infer hidden procurement from missing disclosure.

legalOutcomes.case: Vihaan Kumar v State of Haryana
legalOutcomes.outcome: Arrest invalidated; release and Haryana safeguard directions; chargesheet merits unaffected.

legalOutcomes.case: Mihir Rajesh Shah v State of Maharashtra
legalOutcomes.locator: paras 52–58; printed pp. 46–50 in inspected official PDF
legalOutcomes.outcome: Prospective written-ground schedule across offences; specified urgent oral-first exception.

legalOutcomes.case: Jaskaran Jeet Singh Deol v State of Punjab
legalOutcomes.outcome: Re-arrest after constitutional violation requires supervised judicial process; underlying merits reserved.

methodNotes: Connections assert exactly their relation type. A commercial or oversight link is not an allegation of collusion.
Court holdings are separated from party submissions, investigation merits and later docket status.
Status changes are retained by date; no covert operations, personal device contents or private identifiers are collected.
